history.title: ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED: the convolution ring was exactly conv_k slots wide, but a speculative pass writes TILE rows ahead - so a rejected pass evicted the row the next pass's first convolution still needed. Ring is now (conv_k + TILE).next_power_of_two(), mask-indexed. plain vs spec is now byte-identical over 3 prompts x 300 tokens

gates.G2: parity 6/6 + spec==plain byte-for-byte on 3 prompts x 300 tokens

evidence.root_cause: the pass at position p writes ring slots for p, p+1, p+2; the slot for p+2 is the same slot as p-2 (p+2 = p-2 + conv_k), so the second draft evicted the row for p-2. With k=0 the next pass starts at p+1 and its row 0 convolves over {p-2, p-1, p, p+1}, reading the discarded draft in place of p-2
evidence.why_it_hid: both extra rows are real rows of the same sequence, so the corruption is a one-row-old convolution input - small enough to normally change nothing, which is why I twice mislabelled the resulting divergence as floating-point noise at a near-tie
evidence.fix: ring is (conv_k + TILE).next_power_of_two() = 8 slots, indexed with a mask so the kernel costs exactly what it did before
evidence.method: QW_NO_ACCEPT=1 (force k=0) made the rejection path the only path and turned a rare corruption into divergence at token 4; QW_TILE_CHECK proves the tiled arithmetic is bit-exact (max|dlogit|=0.0). Together they separate wrong arithmetic from wrong state
evidence.tile4: built and tested: correct but strictly worse - acceptance 75.5%->55.6%, tokens/pass 2.51->2.67, materially higher pass cost. TILE=3 stays
evidence.thermal: box throttled from back-to-back model loads (plain decode 87 ms/token vs 24.6 ms in round 031); spec/plain ratio 1.38x unchanged; absolute numbers to be re-measured in a cool window

evidence.change: new kernels conv1d_silu_ring_tile (grid conv_dim*TILE, row r reads ring slot slot0+r) and rmsnorm_nw_tile (grid hk*TILE*NT, threadgroup flattened to (row, head)); forward2's GDN branch is now three phases - qkv per row into its ring slot, then one convolution and two norms for the tile, then the recurrence row by row because it is sequential in the state

evidence.msl_constraint: MSL rejects a kernel that mixes vector thread-position bindings with scalar ones - the flattened 1D grid is a requirement, not a style choice
evidence.ab: order-alternating A/B in one cool window, 4 pairs: 0.987, 0.967, 1.001, 0.953 => median 0.977 (~2.3% faster). Best readings 41.31 (new) vs 40.62 (old) tok/s
evidence.where_time_goes: a pass emits 2.51 tokens in ~61 ms vs a plain step's ~37 ms for one token; the pass moves ~13.5 GB of weights + ~1.9 GB of lm_head (all three rows need logits to verify) + ~1.4 GB of MTP drafts = ~16.8 GB in 61 ms = ~275 GB/s, while the plain step already reaches ~364 GB/s on the same weights, so the speculative pass is NOT at the bandwidth ceiling and has real headroom
evidence.next_suspect: the three-row accumulator in the tiled GEMV costing occupancy; a pass matching the plain step's bandwidth efficiency would land near 60 tok/s

history.next: attack the tiled GEMV's bandwidth efficiency: measure occupancy/register pressure for the k=3 kernel, try wider threadgroups or splitting the accumulator, and re-run the order-alternating A/B. Keep the byte-identical gate (now asserting token counts) as the correctness gate

history.title: GDN qkv projection converted to one tiled launch into a qkv_cur staging buffer, with the convolution reading in-flight rows from it and each layer copying its own rows to the ring. Bit-identical (same group walk/order/simd_sum as k=1) and worth ~2.2% in an order-alternating A/B; best 24.15 ms/token (~41.4 tok/s)

gates.G2: parity 6/6 + spec==plain byte-for-byte, 2 prompts x 300 tokens, length asserted

evidence.change: in_qkv is projected once per pass with the k=3 kernel into qkv_cur[TILE][conv_dim] instead of once per row into the ring (3x the weight reads, ~3 GB/pass, 19% of traffic). The tile convolution reads rows with pos >= pos0 from qkv_cur and older ones from the ring; each layer then memcpys its own TILE rows into their ring slots
evidence.why_safe: Q4_GEMV_KS is bit-identical per row to the k=1 kernel - same g = lane; g < n_groups; g += 32 walk, same Q4_WORDS_PER_GROUP unpack order, same simd_sum(acc[t]) per row - so a tile launch performs exactly the operations in exactly the order three k=1 launches would
evidence.bug_i_wrote: the first version copied accepted rows into the ring at end-of-pass from spec_step. WRONG because qkv_cur is one scratch buffer shared by every layer: by then it holds the last layer's rows, so every other layer's ring got that layer's data. Diverged at token 4, the same signature as round 035's ring bug; the byte-identical gate caught it in one run. The copy now happens inside each layer's own block right after its convolution
evidence.why_not_acceptance_dependent: k is only known after the logits are read, i.e. after the whole forward is encoded, so the copy cannot be restricted to the k+1 surviving rows. Copying all TILE rows is what the old per-row projection did and the ring is wide enough to absorb it
evidence.ab: order-alternating A/B, 4 pairs, one cool window: 0.981, 0.976, 1.020, 0.955 => median paired ratio 0.978 (~2.2%)
evidence.implication: far less than the ~2 GB of saved traffic implies, so the pass is issue-bound in the tiled GEMV rather than bandwidth-bound
evidence.next_candidates: the attention layer's per-row kv_append, attn_scores, attn_out and gate_mul - 4 per row, 12 per attention layer, ~190 per pass

history.next: batch the attention layer's per-row launches (kv_append, attn_scores, attn_out, gate_mul) over the tile rows the same way the convolution and norms were batched, then re-run oracle parity, the byte-identical gate with length assertions, and the order-alternating A/B

history.title: FLAGGED (unresolved): one verify run reported parity 5/6; not reproducible in 13 subsequent runs on both binaries, and the change under test was incapable of altering arithmetic. The failing run was the last command of a shell invocation that had just run build+fmt+clippy+cargo test (which loads the model on the same GPU); no other gate run has shared a window with a build-and-test sweep

evidence.observation: a single verify run printed parity: 5/6 while spec==plain stayed byte-identical over 300 tokens on the same build
evidence.why_it_cannot_be_the_change: (t - 1) as i32 -> t - 1 where t is already i32, plus removal of two struct fields nothing read
evidence.reproduction_attempts: 13 runs total (6 across the two binaries, then 10 more on the committed build) all 6/6
evidence.not_captured: the failing case identity was lost because that run only grepped the summary line
evidence.hypothesis: resource contention with a failure mode that is not validated - device buffers are written without error checking - since it was the only gate run issued in the same shell window as cargo build/fmt/clippy/test, and cargo test loads and runs the model on the same GPU

history.next: reproduce the intermittent parity failure deliberately: loop verify many times while recording the failing case identity and the load average, and if it reappears under contention, add a GPU completion/error check after the gate's forwards so a device fault surfaces as an error instead of a wrong token

history.title: Contention experiment: 5 verify runs under load 3.7-6.8 all read 6/6, so the round-037 anomaly did not reproduce (1 in ~19 runs, still open). Also found and then measured-away a batching idea: kv_append/gate_mul batch over the tile byte-identically once k's row stride (key_dim) is distinguished from v's (nkv*hd), but run 5.7% SLOWER because the flattened row decode costs an integer division per thread in kernels that only do a couple of loads. No code change

gates.G2: parity 6/6 + spec==plain byte-for-byte on the restored tree

evidence.contention_experiment: 30 verify runs in a loop with full output per run and loadavg per run; the 5 that completed on the unmodified binary (load 3.7-6.8) all read 6/6. The loop was then contaminated by a rebuild and killed
evidence.plain_path_stable_under_load: idle plain vs loaded plain: 0 differences over 300 tokens with a concurrent generation running, so the plain decode path is not fragile
evidence.latent_trap: scratch.k is shared by two branches whose rows differ in width: the GDN branch defines key_dim = hk*dk while the attention branch's k projection is nkv*hd. The attention dispatch used the local key_dim as the row offset while scratch.pv used nkv*hd, so any refactor that treats the two names as the same number reads the wrong row - and the symptom is a spec-vs-plain divergence at a drifting token index, not obvious corruption. This cost most of the round
evidence.batched_but_slower: with both strides explicit, kv_append and gate_mul batch over the tile correctly and byte-identically, removing 4 launches per attention layer (64 per pass). Measured 1.041 and 1.073 paired ratios => 5.7% slower, reverted
evidence.why_slower: batching requires the row to be decoded from the flattened index - one integer division per thread - while gate_mul does one load, one exp and one store, and kv_append two loads and two stores. The division costs more than the launch it removes, the opposite of the convolution and norms in rounds 036-037 where each thread does enough work to hide the decode
evidence.implication: the cheap batching lever is exhausted; two rounds of batching bought ~2% each and dispatch time is only ~6.5 ms of a 61 ms pass, so the tiled GEMV's issue cost is the remaining lever, not dispatch count

history.next: attack the tiled GEMV's issue cost directly rather than the dispatch count: measure whether the k=3 kernel's per-row epilogue (three simd_sum reductions plus three stores per thread) or the nibble unpack dominates, e.g. by timing a k=3 launch whose rows write to the same location, and only then consider restructuring the reduction. Keep the dispatch-count work for the two rmsnorm_ws pairs and rope pairs, which are the only remaining per-row launches with enough per-thread work to amortise a row decode

history.title: Pass census (1922 dispatches, only 497 GEMV) and two copy folds into existing kernels: state snapshot into gdn_step and ring update into the tile convolution. 1922 -> 1634 dispatches, 2.0% faster (4/4 interleaved pairs), byte-identical. Also cleared a bench trap (rows=0 uses the runtime-k kernel, so the apparent 2x from row blocking was an artifact) and found the machine is on battery + Low Power Mode, which caps absolute throughput 2.5x

gates.G2: parity 6/6 + spec==plain byte-for-byte, 300 tokens, plain byte-identical to the previous build
gates.G3: 2.0% via interleaved A/B (4/4 pairs); absolute numbers unusable, machine on battery + Low Power Mode

evidence.census: `QW_DISPATCH_HIST` on a real decode pass: 1922 dispatches, q4_gemv_k3 only 497 (26%). The other 1425 are copy_off 288, gdn_step 144, rmsnorm_gated 144, rmsnorm 129, rmsnorm_nw_tile 96, rmsnorm_s 96, rope_partial 96, ewise_add 128, silu_mul 64, conv1d_silu_ring_tile 48, and 48 each of kv_append/attn_scores_softmax/attn_out/gate_mul. The engine's own split: draft 5.9 ms/pass, verify 89.6 ms/pass
evidence.bench_trap: bench --tokens 3 with rows=0 calls QLinear::kernel_k() = q4_gemv_k, the RUNTIME-k kernel whose token loop is not unrolled; rows=1 selects q4_gemv_k3, the unrolled specialisation, with an identical grid. The engine already uses the unrolled one, so the 78.70 vs 38.19 ms '2x from row blocking' was measuring a kernel the model never runs, and round 039's '~62% of single-row bandwidth' claim rested on it
evidence.corrected_gemv: unrolled both sides: k=1 31.33 ms (460 GB/s), k=3 38.19 ms (377 GB/s), marginal row 3.43 ms = 57.6 GFLOP at ~16.8 TFLOP/s, i.e. essentially the fp32 ALU peak. The three-row GEMV is already close to optimal and the 6.86 ms spent on rows 2-3 cannot be removed without packed/tensor-core math, which would risk oracle parity. The 50 tok/s target must come from the 1425 non-GEMV dispatches
evidence.change: folded two copy_off launches into the kernels that already hold the data: (1) gdn_step now writes the row-end state snapshot itself (buffers 13/14, guarded by snap_on), removing a whole-state copy per row AND its read (~450 MB/pass); (2) conv1d_silu_ring_tile writes its own ring slot, safe because every window read in that dispatch is for pos < pos0, at least three slots behind. A/B: 4 pairs, ratios 0.9756/0.9845/0.9687/0.9917, median 0.9801 => 2.0%
evidence.power_trap: mid-round absolute throughput collapsed from 23.6 to 58.5 ms/token and stayed: pmset reports drawing from Battery Power while discharging with powermode 1 (Low Power). Three runs then read 58.53/58.54/58.25 ms - stable and 2.5x slower than on mains. Absolute tok/s is only comparable within one power state; a 50 tok/s claim needs mains power with Low Power Mode off
evidence.stray_process: a leftover `qwen38 serve --addr 127.0.0.1:8088` from an earlier round (old CLI flag) was holding 18.7 GB; killed

history.next: keep cutting the 1425 non-GEMV dispatches, in order of size: ewise_add 128 (fuse the residual add into the following rmsnorm), rmsnorm_gated 144 and rmsnorm_s 96 (batch over TILE - these are heavy reduction kernels, so unlike kv_append/gate_mul in round 038 the row decode should amortise), rope_partial 96, and merging the MLP gate/up GEMVs (64). Re-derive the absolute tok/s only on mains power with Low Power Mode off

history.title: Discovered q4_gemv_kr never implemented row blocking ((void)R), implemented true row blocking (R=2..8 + uint4 variants) plus a paired bench sweep mode, and found it ~5% SLOWER end-to-end (8 interleaved pairs, 6/8 slower); reverted. Also corrected round 040: the marginal row cost is superlinear (+1.20/+3.83/+6.00 ms), so the sweep is latency- not FLOP-bound, and the measurement environment (battery + Low Power Mode) makes both absolute numbers and best-of-N/B paired micro-sweeps unreliable

gates.G2: parity 6/6 + spec==plain byte-for-byte 300 tokens, plain identical to round 037
gates.G3: row blocking rejected: median paired ratio 1.0481 over 8 interleaved pairs, 6/8 slower

evidence.marginal_row: with the correct unrolled kernels: k=1 27.94, k=2 29.14 (+1.20), k=3 32.97 (+3.83), k=4 38.97 (+6.00) ms. Superlinear, and k=3 moves 86.4 GFLOP in 32.97 ms = 2.6 TFLOP/s, an order of magnitude below peak, so the sweep is latency/memory limited - round 040's 'marginal row is at the fp32 ALU peak' was wrong
evidence.kr_never_blocked: crates/qw-metal/src/msl.rs:145 is `(void)R;` - q4_gemv_kr discards R and is only q4_gemv_k with uint4 weight loads. Round 039's 'row blocking was falsified' conclusion rested on a kernel that does not block
evidence.implementation: Q4_GEMV_KS_R(NAME, NK, R): R output rows per threadgroup, x loaded once per group and held across all R rows, dividing the x load traffic (which is out_dim times the input size) by R while reading each row's weights once. Per-row accumulation order is bit-identical to q4_gemv_k3. Also Q4_GEMV_KS_U4 (16-byte weight loads) and `bench --rows 9` (paired sweep of candidates vs baseline in one process)
evidence.sweep_flips: run A R4 0.8866 (35/40); run B R4 0.9516 (32/40) with R6 1.3283 (1/40) and R8 1.2058 (2/40); run C R4 0.8734 (59/60); run D (same binary, same command, 40 s later) R4 1.0340 (18/60). R6/R8 spill badly, and including a much-slower variant poisons the paired baseline within a round
evidence.e2e_verdict: 8 interleaved pairs vs the round-040 binary: ratios 0.9823/1.7597/1.0465/1.1875/0.9040/1.0559/1.0478/1.0483, median 1.0481, 6/8 slower. Every pair whose baseline was not an outlier (58-66 ms/token) has R=4 slower by 4-19%. Reverted
evidence.why_sweep_disagrees: the sweep reuses ONE input buffer for all 497 linears, so x stays cache-hot and the traffic row blocking removes is understated; in the model the same kernel also covers linears with tiny out_f (GDN a/b projections are 48 rows), where blocking leaves the grid nearly empty
evidence.environment: battery + powermode 1 all round. Same binary, same sweep: 27.9 / 33.0 / 58.5 / 70.6 / 113.5 ms across the session; one variant's samples inside one run spanned 65-294 ms. Absolute tok/s is not comparable across sessions, and relative claims need >=6 tightly interleaved model-level pairs. A 50 tok/s verification needs mains power with Low Power Mode off

history.next: Do not spend more rounds on ~5% kernel experiments until the machine is on mains power: they cannot be resolved. The solid, measurement-independent facts to build on are the 1634-dispatch census (only 497 GEMV) and the superlinear marginal-row curve. The largest non-GEMV blocks remain ewise_add 128, rmsnorm_gated 144, rmsnorm 129, rmsnorm_nw_tile 96, rmsnorm_s 96, rope_partial 96; fusing the residual add into the following rmsnorm and batching the per-row reduction kernels over TILE are the next candidates. Ask the user to plug in and turn off Low Power Mode before any further throughput claim

history.title: Found and fixed a reading error in the engine's own split report (it divided by drafts, not passes), then ablated the forward with new dispatch filters: the 1137 non-GEMV dispatches are worth only 8.6 ms (7%), while the 497-dispatch GEMV sweep is 93%. But the same 497 dispatches cost 3.5x more in situ (113.8 ms) than in the isolated bench (32.6 ms), and four explanations were refuted: CPU encoding is 1.1-1.9 ms, barrier()'s 1090 encoder splits cost nothing (1 encoder gives no gain), dependencies are absent in the filtered run, and per-linear x buffers change nothing

gates.G3: no speedup claimed; four hypotheses measured and killed

evidence.report_bug: gen.rs:387 divides t_draft/t_pass by `drafts` (= passes*(TILE-1)), not by passes, so the printed ms/pass is really ms per draft. True split: draft 9.9 + verify 133.1 + tail 3 = ~146 ms/pass, matching the wall clock. Round 041's 'half the pass is unaccounted' was an artifact
evidence.tail: the untimed tail (commit_row + promote_hidden + post-accept redraft) is only 1.7-4.8 ms
evidence.ablation: QW_ONLY_KERNEL/QW_SKIP_KERNEL dispatch filters added to CommandBatch::encode. k=2 forward: full 122.40 ms, only q4_gemv 113.78, skip gdn_step 117.17, skip rmsnorm family 120.43, skip conv1d 122.92, skip attn 123.43. So all 1137 non-GEMV dispatches = 8.6 ms = 7%
evidence.in_situ_gap: same 497 dispatches, same grid (out_f*32, tg 32), same kernels/weights: in situ 55.08-64.48 ms (k=1) and 113.78 ms (k=3) vs isolated bench 27.39-36.24 ms (k=1) and 32.62 ms (k=3)
evidence.refuted: (1) CPU command encoding is 1.14-1.86 ms for 1634 dispatches, not the cost; (2) barrier() ends the encoder (1090 encoders per pass) and using ONE encoder changes nothing (61.64 vs 55.08 on the filtered run, 63.24 vs 64.48 on the full); (3) the filtered run has no producers/dependencies at all and is still slow; (4) QW_X_PER_LINEAR=1 (a distinct x per linear) gives 33.48 ms vs 36.24 - no slowdown
evidence.barrier_impl: barrier() is not a memory barrier: it calls enc.end_encoding(), so the batch has 1090 encoder boundaries per pass. Measured to cost nothing
evidence.instruments: QW_ENCODE_TIME=1 (CPU encode ms, commit+wait ms, dispatches, encoders per batch); QW_ONLY_KERNEL=<substr>/QW_SKIP_KERNEL=<substr>; QW_X_PER_LINEAR=1 (bench); QW_NO_ENC_SPLIT=1 (unsafe timing bound)

history.next: The open question is why the identical 497 sweep dispatches cost 3.5x more inside a pass than isolated, now that CPU encoding, encoder splitting, dependencies and x locality are all excluded. Leading remaining candidates: DRAM access locality of the dispatch order (the bench walks linears in sorted-name order, the model walks them in layer order), the effect of real activation data versus the bench's constant 0.01, and GPU clock state during a long measurement versus a short one. If the in-situ sweep reached the bench's rate the forward would drop from ~122 ms to ~40 ms, which would clear 50 tok/s outright - so this is now the only question worth budget. Absolute tok/s still needs mains power with Low Power Mode off

history.title: Answered round 042's open question: the in-situ/isolated gap is GPU clock throttling under sustained load (3-5x), not anything about the kernels. Added QW_BENCH_BURN and found the throttle plateaus after 20-30 s (stable to 0.05%), which finally makes A/B measurement reproducible on this machine. Added a steady-state throughput window to `gen` (0.5% spread over 3 runs). Split verify (forward2 126-128 ms, logits pulls only 2.73 ms so GPU argmax is not worth it). Rejected row blocking at the plateau with 60 paired rounds. Concluded the sweep (77% of a pass) saturates both throttled memory bandwidth and throttled ALU issue, so no code change can reach it on battery

evidence.throttle: QW_BENCH_BURN added to bench. Same 497-dispatch k=3 sweep: cold 38.42/32.49 ms (two fresh processes), after 3 s of load 110.60 ms, after 10 s 160.57 ms. The round-042 'in situ is 3.5x slower' gap is entirely power management
evidence.plateau: burn 5 s -> 156.2 ms/sweep then 206.76 measured (degrading); 15 s -> 144.2 then 110.63; 30 s -> 112.8 then 113.12; 45 s -> 113.6 then 113.18. Stable to 0.05% across processes; 120 s idle restores 36.41 ms
evidence.reproducible_metric: gen now reports a steady-state window over the last third of tokens: 18.48/18.43/18.38 tok/s (54.1/54.3/54.4 ms/token), 2.69 tokens/pass, 0.5% spread over 3 runs. 18.4 tok/s battery vs 42.4 tok/s mains on the same binary = 2.3x
evidence.verify_split: set_tokens 0.03 ms | forward2 126-128 ms | 3x(logits pull + argmax) 2.73 ms. GPU-side argmax would save ~2%, not worth doing
evidence.plateau_sweep: k=1 84.10 ms (171 GB/s), k=2 97.88, k=3 113.15 (127 GB/s). Fit a+b*k: fixed 69.6 ms for the 14.41 GB weight stream (207 GB/s) + a flat 14.5 ms per row
evidence.row_blocking_rejected: at the plateau, 60 tightly paired rounds with alternating order: R2 ratio 1.0690 wins 3/60, R3 1.0387 wins 7/60, R4 1.0266 wins 15/60 - slower at every factor, and now with a trustworthy measurement
evidence.conclusion: the sweep is 77% of a pass and saturates both throttled memory bandwidth (207 vs 440 GB/s cold) and throttled ALU issue (14.5 ms/row). Weights are irreducible at 4-bit, so no code change reaches it in this power state

history.next: The 50 tok/s target must be worked and verified on mains with Low Power Mode off; on battery the honest figure is 18.4 tok/s steady-state, now reproducible. When mains is available: re-measure the steady-state number, then re-open the sweep with the plateau protocol - the specific question is whether a mains sweep reaches ~500 GB/s (recoverable to 50 tok/s) or is already at the practical peak (in which case the remaining 23% of the pass, not the sweep, is the only place left)

next: convert the GDN qkv projection to the tile kernel: project into a contiguous qkv_cur[TILE][conv_dim] with one k=3 launch (bit-identical to three k=1 launches - same group walk, same Q4_WORDS_PER_GROUP order, same simd_sum per row, which is why QW_TILE_CHECK reads exactly 0.0), have the tile convolution read its own rows from qkv_cur and older rows from the ring, and at the end of the pass memcpy the k+1 accepted rows into their ring slots. One launch instead of three and ~2 GB less redundant weight traffic per pass (~12% of the pass), far more than the ~2.3% round 036 bought. Needs the ring bookkeeping reworked, so give it a full round. Then re-run: oracle parity, the byte-identical gate with token counts asserted, and the order-alternating A/B
